chunks: Al-Hasan b. Muhammad b. Yahya b. al-Hasan b. Jafar b. Ubaydullah b. al-Husayn b. Ali b. al-Husayn b. Ali b. Abi Talib (peace be upon them) narrated to us. He said: My grandfather Yahya b. al-Hasan b. Jafar b. Ubaydullah narrated to me. He said: Ibrahim b. Ali and al-Hasan b. Yahya narrated to me. They both said: Nasr b. Muzahim narrated to us from Abu Khalid from Zayd b. Ali from his forefathers from Ali (peace be upon them).

He said: I was given ten characteristics by the Messenger of Allah (blessings of Allah be upon him and his family). He did not give them to anyone before me, nor will anyone be given them after me. He said to me: O Ali! You are my brother in this world and in the Hereafter. You are the nearest of the people to me in position on the Day of Resurrection. My house and your house in Paradise face one another, like the house of two brothers. You are the deputy, you are the friend [of Allah], and you are the vizier. Your enemy is my enemy, and my enemy is the enemy of Allah. Your friend is my friend, and my friend is the friend of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

key_terms.الوزير: The vizier/minister -- political title affirming Ali's advisory role
key_terms.الوصي: The deputy/successor -- title establishing Ali's legitimate succession
key_terms.الولي: The friend/authority -- title indicating divine friendship and authority
key_terms.عشر: Ten -- referring to ten exclusive characteristics given to Ali

ai.seo_question: What are the ten characteristics the Prophet gave exclusively to Ali according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith, Ali (as) narrates that the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) bestowed upon him ten unique characteristics not given to anyone before or after him. These include: being the Prophet's brother in this world and the Hereafter, being the nearest to him on the Day of Resurrection, having adjacent houses in Paradise, being designated as the deputy (wasi), friend of Allah (wali), and vizier. The Prophet also declared that Ali's enemies are his enemies and Allah's enemies, and Ali's friends are his friends and Allah's friends. This tradition is significant in Shia theology for establishing Ali's unique spiritual and political authority.
